newsitem.title: UK: Safeway profits rise, current sales ahead.
newsitem.headline: Safeway profits rise, current sales ahead.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc checked in a seven percent rise in half-year profits as expected on Thursday and said current sales were up five percent.
Pretax profits rose to 228.2 million pounds ($383.5 million) from 213.7 million pounds previously, compared with forecasts of between 228 to 231 million pounds.
The company said food retailing in Britain remained "fiercely competitive," but added it felt in a good position to deliver growth and value for shareholders.

It paid out an interim dividend of 4.4 pence per share, up from 4.05 pence per share previously. Safeway shares were flat in early trading at 371 pence, however, as the results were towards the lower end of expectations.
Safeway said sales in existing stores were up five percent in the first five weeks of the second half after gaining 5.1 percent in the first half, with food inflation "particularly subdued."

The company said gross margins had run slightly down on last year in recent weeks, driven by "our immediate and vigorous response to a number of significant marketing and pricing initiatives launched by competitors."
Safeway, which targets the family shopper, said market share rose to 7.8 percent in the first half from 7.5 percent a year ago.
The company said it would be opening 450,000 square feet of new space in each of the next two years, adding some 5,200 jobs.
Safeway said its focus was now on "continuing to build the Safeway brand...and leading the industry in making shopping easier for customers." ($1=.5950 Pound)
